pr.title: Point the relay at the hosted service on login, with keys that project hosted credentials asks it for
pr.head: e32bb249362d6512bda823bc8b28b7449927fd9f

summary: Projector's relay carries agent messages between your machines and your peers' machines. It can run through a GitHub repository or an S3 bucket you own. A hosted Projector service can now run an S3 relay for you, so you need neither. This pull request is the CLI's side of that: it signs the relay in to the hosted relay and gets it short-lived keys.

1. Login points the relay at the hosted relay. After project hosted login registers your agent.key, it writes agent.relay = "s3://projector", agent.s3_endpoint, and agent.s3_profile = "projector-hosted" to ~/.projector.toml. It also writes an AWS profile whose credential_process runs project hosted credentials. When your user file already names another relay, login leaves it alone and names project hosted relay, which switches.
  2. project hosted credentials asks the service for keys. It posts the account token and a per-machine ID and prints the service's JSON unchanged, which is the form a credential_process prints. The relay's S3 client already runs such a command and refreshes the keys 5 minutes before they expire.
  3. Logout undoes what login wrote, but only the values that still hold what login wrote.
  4. A named profile now signs ahead of environment keys. When agent.s3_profile names a profile, the S3 client now skips AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID in the environment, as AWS's SDKs do. Without that change, keys left in a developer's shell would sign hosted requests, and the hosted relay would refuse them.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Relay: where agent messages travel, set by agent.relay.
  • User layer: ~/.projector.toml. Nearer .projector.toml files, in a directory or a repository, override it key by key.
  • credential_process: an AWS profile option that names a command printing temporary keys as JSON.
  • Machine ID: 16 random bytes kept in the state directory. Paired machines share agent.key, so the key alone cannot tell the service which machine is asking.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
The first Projector review of e32bb24 requested changes, with two findings:

  • Login checks only the user layer before it writes the hosted endpoint and profile. A nearer layer's S3 agent.relay then picks those two up and moves to the hosted store.
  • On Windows, a project path that contains a space produces a credential_process that the S3 client cannot start.

groups.title: Which credentials sign
groups.kicker: The S3 client's credential order, and the relay's reading of a 402
intro: The relay's S3 client finds keys in a fixed order: first the environment, then the profile's files, then the profile's credential_process. Now, when agent.s3_profile names a profile, the client skips the environment, so the hosted profile's keys sign even when your shell holds AWS keys of your own. When the profile comes only from AWS_PROFILE or default, the environment still comes first.

The relay already turns off with a notice when its credentials fail or S3 answers 403. Now it also turns off on a 402, which the hosted relay sends when a subscription lapses while keys are still valid, and the notice tells you to run project hosted subscribe.

files.note: Provider.find skips environment keys when the profile is named, and sign_in_fix answers project hosted login for the hosted profile.

checks.text: Finding from the review: on Windows, this file splits a credential_process with shlex.split(posix=False), here and in run_process. That split keeps the quotes that list2cmdline put around a path with a space, so run_process cannot start the command that hosted.credentials_command writes.

files.note: store_error reads a 402 as a lapse whose fix is project hosted subscribe.

groups.title: The hosted.relay setting
groups.kicker: Where the hosted relay's store lives
intro: hosted.relay names the hosted relay's S3 endpoint, https://relay.projector.bot by default, and login writes it to agent.s3_endpoint. It counts as a destination, like hosted.url, so a value in a committed file applies only once you allow it. It accepts the same https:// form as agent.s3_endpoint, so s3_endpoint now takes the name of the setting it reports errors for.

files.note: Adds hosted.relay to SETTINGS and DESTINATIONS, and its default, HOSTED_RELAY.

groups.title: Login, relay, credentials, and logout
groups.kicker: What the hosted commands write, ask for, and remove
intro: use_relay holds the same lock as every other change to ~/.projector.toml. It writes the AWS profile first, then the three settings. Without switch, which only project hosted relay passes, a user file that already sets any of the three to another value stays as it is.

The AWS config file gets a line edit, not a rewrite: find_profile locates the hosted profile and its credential_process, and write_profiles writes the file only when configparser reads it back with nothing changed outside that profile.

credentials prints the service's body byte for byte. When the service answers 402, the error leaves out the service's own words, because the S3 client reads a last line that says "expired" as an AWS sign-in to renew.

files.note: The new commands' logic: the relay settings, the AWS profile edit, the machine ID, and the credentials call.

checks.text: Finding from the review: the check that a relay is already chosen reads only ~/.projector.toml, but the relay reads agent.s3_endpoint and agent.s3_profile from any layer. A nearer layer that sets agent.relay = "s3://acme-agents/relay" moves to https://relay.projector.bot/acme-agents/relay after login. The review reproduced this in a temporary home.
Finding from the review: on Windows, a path with a space is quoted here with list2cmdline, and s3.Provider.run_process cannot start the quoted command.

machine_id links a temporary file into place, so two first runs at once keep one ID. A file system without hard links falls back to a replace, where two concurrent first runs can each keep a different ID.

files.note: Wires up hosted relay and hosted credentials, and passes the relay settings to login and logout.

groups.kicker: The new section in the CLI reference
intro: docs/cli.md adds hosted.relay to the settings table, the new credential order, and a section called "Relay through the hosted service". The section shows what login writes, when it leaves your relay alone, and what logout removes.
